parsed.why: No trans-specific offence; hate-crime law covers gender identity and police must use identified gender, but enforcement weak, complaints ignored, attacks unpunished. Latest documented attack 2014; entrenched heteronormative hostility with thin remedy.

Fresh criminalisation (2–5 years) with stated deportation of foreign nationals, promotion ban, military rule, no rule of law, no protections, no remedy, no enforcement record: statutory discretionary exposure dominates.

No criminalisation and strong court/community positives, but recent documented harassment and discrimination against visibly trans people in provincial cities and rising political hostility with death threats; recourse thin.

Decriminalised with court reading sex discrimination to cover gender identity; no criminal exposure, no documented targeting, no transit restrictions. Only social/religious hostility and no local recognition mechanism — resident-facing gaps.

No criminal statute, but no protections, no functioning judicial remedy, documented hostility to visible LGBTI people, unresolved activist death and camp harassment; pending 2017 bills unverified. Thin recourse.
